explanation: Jacopo Peri's Dafne was staged in Florence around 1598, and his Euridice of 1600 is among the earliest operas whose music survives. Shakespeare died in 1616.

claims.text: Jacopo Peri's Dafne, generally regarded as the first opera, was staged in Florence around 1598.
Peri's Euridice, first performed in Florence in 1600, is among the earliest operas whose music survives.

Argued against the key: Dafne dates from 1597 or 1598 and Euridice from 1600; even 1600 is 16 years before 1616, past the 10-year guard. Counterintuitive is true, so both label claims are high under C26. Volatility: evergreen; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: Shakespeare and opera are known worldwide. Style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words. Myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json, no hit. Mystery: not applicable to a practice item. Encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: Dafne's music is mostly lost and its exact year is given as 1597 or 1598, so the label claim and display say 'around 1598'. p.lang.0273 (a dictionary, b02 of Language & Words) also uses Shakespeare's death as its anchor, for a different fact; the labels here are worded apart from it.
